teaching_card.title: Angles and Polygons (Medium)
teaching_card.body: Most angle questions reduce to a few facts: angles on a line sum to 180°, around a point to 360°, in a triangle to 180°. Parallel lines cut by a transversal create equal (corresponding, alternate) and supplementary (same-side) pairs, and a polygon with n sides has interior angles summing to 180(n − 2).
key_points: Triangle angles sum to 180°; an exterior angle equals the two remote interior angles.
Parallel lines + transversal: corresponding and alternate angles are equal; same-side interior angles sum to 180°.
Polygon interior sum = 180(n − 2); exterior angles always sum to 360°.
teaching_card.worked_example: Regular hexagon: 180·4/6 = 120° per interior angle; exterior 360/6 = 60°.

screens.title: Angle pairs and parallel lines
screens.body: Complementary angles sum to 90°, supplementary to 180°, and vertical angles (across an X) are equal. When a transversal crosses parallel lines, every angle is either equal to a given angle or supplementary to it: decide which by whether the two angles 'look the same' (both acute or both obtuse).
key_points: With parallels, every angle is x or 180 − x.

screens.title: Triangles
screens.body: The three angles add to 180°. In an isosceles triangle the base angles are equal, so the vertex angle is 180 − 2·(base angle). An exterior angle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles. When angles are given as expressions, add them, set the sum to 180, and solve for x — then answer the question actually asked (often the angle, not x).
key_points: Exterior angle = sum of remote interior angles.
Solve for x, then compute the angle.

screens.title: Polygons
screens.body: Split a polygon into n − 2 triangles from one vertex: the interior angles sum to 180(n − 2). The exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360°, so a regular n-gon has exterior angles of 360/n and interior angles of 180 − 360/n. To find n from an interior angle, use the exterior angle: n = 360/(180 − interior).

screens.title: Try the moves
screens.body: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°: exterior = 30°, so n = 360/30 = 12 sides. Angles (2x + 10)°, (3x)°, and 50° in a triangle: 5x + 60 = 180 → x = 24, so the angles are 58°, 72°, 50°.
